entries.title: openai/openai-agents-python
entries.current_signal: Current README presents it as a lightweight multi-agent workflow SDK with tools, guardrails, human-in-the-loop, sessions, tracing, MCP, and sandbox agents.
entries.learn: Tool contracts, guardrails, handoffs, sessions, tracing, and human approval as first-class objects.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Controller/tools/trace vocabulary without making the LLM the source of truth.
entries.selection_guidance: Use as runtime vocabulary and eventual SDK path; keep deterministic mode for offline eval.
entries.design_note: I borrowed the explicit tools/guardrails/tracing model, but kept a local controller protocol so evals still run without an API key.

entries.title: Anthropic: Building effective agents
entries.current_signal: The article distinguishes workflows from agents, recommends simple solutions first, and emphasizes well-documented agent-computer interfaces.
entries.learn: When to use workflows, when to add agent autonomy, and why tool design is part of agent design.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Start with a deterministic workflow, then add model-driven control where eval evidence justifies it.
entries.selection_guidance: Use as the main architecture explanation in design notes.
entries.design_note: The project starts as a workflow on purpose: it locks down source provenance, state, and eval before introducing model autonomy.

entries.title: langchain-ai/langgraph
entries.current_signal: GitHub README points to durable execution that resumes after failures and human-in-the-loop state inspection or modification.
entries.learn: State graph semantics, checkpointing, long-running execution, and human review of mutable state.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Typed state graph with stop-after, checkpoint-on-error, and resume paths.
entries.selection_guidance: Adopt when persistence backend and concurrent long-running runs become real product needs.
entries.design_note: I implemented the minimal state graph first, so I can explain exactly what LangGraph would replace.

entries.title: Model Context Protocol
entries.current_signal: GitHub org frames MCP as a protocol for integrating LLM applications with external data sources, with specification docs and official SDKs.
entries.learn: Tool/data/workflow protocol boundaries, server/client separation, discovery, and permission surfaces.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Tool manifest and approval policy designed so local tools can later become MCP tools.
entries.selection_guidance: Use for Phase 6, after local tools and approval semantics are stable.
entries.design_note: I did not start by shipping an MCP server; I first made tool contracts explicit enough that an MCP adapter has a clean boundary.

entries.title: vibrantlabsai/ragas
entries.current_signal: Docs position Ragas as a move from vibe checks to systematic evaluation loops and list agent/tool-use metrics such as tool call accuracy and agent goal accuracy.
entries.learn: Evaluation datasets, metrics, experiment loops, and separating retrieval, grounding, and tool-use quality.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Case corpora, guardrail checks, audit rubric, and naive baseline comparison.
entries.selection_guidance: Use the evaluation mindset now; keep heavyweight evaluator integrations optional.
entries.design_note: The project is not judged by one demo prompt; it has fixed corpora, guardrail checks, and baseline delta.

entries.title: crewAIInc/crewAI
entries.current_signal: README distinguishes autonomous Crews from production-ready event-driven Flows with fine-grained control and state management.
entries.learn: How to decide between multi-agent role collaboration and controlled workflow execution.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Avoid decorative multi-agent design; use controlled flow unless role decomposition earns its complexity.
entries.selection_guidance: Study the crews/flows distinction; do not use multi-agent roles as a portfolio gimmick.
entries.design_note: I can explain why this project is not multi-agent yet: the current bottleneck is eval and provenance.

entries.title: OpenHands/OpenHands
entries.current_signal: GitHub repository describes OpenHands as AI-driven development with CLI and developer-tooling scope.
entries.learn: Workspace-agent product surfaces: files, commands, long tasks, local runtime, and user-facing UI.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Generated artifact index and local dashboard instead of a single notebook or chat transcript.
entries.selection_guidance: Borrow product-shape lessons when adding experiment execution or UI.
entries.design_note: A serious agent project needs an inspectable product surface, not only an implementation path.

entries.title: huggingface/smolagents
entries.current_signal: README emphasizes agents that think in code, minimal abstractions, and sandboxed execution options.
entries.learn: Why code actions need sandboxing and why small abstractions are easier to inspect.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Keep the local loop small, typed, and auditable before adding remote execution.
entries.selection_guidance: Use as a warning that code/experiment execution must come with sandbox and permission scope.
entries.design_note: The project deliberately plans experiment execution later, after source and permission gates exist.

entries.title: microsoft/autogen
entries.current_signal: README now directs new users to Microsoft Agent Framework and describes AutoGen as maintenance mode.
entries.learn: Multi-agent API history, migration risk, and why framework status must be checked before choosing a stack.
entries.borrowed_pattern: Use AutoGen as historical reference, not as the primary dependency for a new portfolio project.
entries.selection_guidance: Do not build new core architecture on a maintenance-mode framework.
entries.design_note: I checked current project status before choosing what to borrow; not every popular repo should be adopted.

project_fit_summary: The strongest project story is not framework adoption. It is a source-grounded research workflow with explicit tools, state, eval, audit, approval, and reproducible artifacts. Frameworks are used as design references and future integration paths.
